title: CONFIRMED (high): client-supplied X-Request-ID is stored verbatim in the UNIQUE call_logs.request_id, and any reused value aborts the whole chunked audit INSERT — silently destroying other tenants' call audit for the entire 200 ms flush
primary_fix_site: backend/internal/gateway/gateway.go:84 (unvalidated client value) + backend/internal/model/model.go:248 (uniqueIndex on it) + backend/internal/audit/audit.go:67-70 (discard-instead-of-retry)
evidence: Every citation verified byte-for-byte. gateway.go:84 `if v := strings.TrimSpace(c.GetHeader("X-Request-ID")); v != "" && len(v) <= 128 {` (only other branch is `return newRequestID()` at :87); gateway.go:306 `reqID := resolveRequestID(c)`; gateway.go:311 `requestID: reqID, start: start, keyID: apiKey.ID, keyLabel: apiKey.Name,`; gateway.go:272 `RequestID: p.requestID,`; model.go:248 `RequestID string `gorm:"uniqueIndex;size:40" json:"request_id"``, index materialised because db.go:63 `gdb.AutoMigrate(model.AllModels()...)` and model.go:301 lists `&CallLog{}`. Writer: audit.go:60 `ticker := time.NewTicker(200 * time.Millisecond)`, :62 `batch := make([]*model.CallLog, 0, 64)`, :67 `if err := l.db.CreateInBatches(batch, 50).Error; err != nil {`, :68 `log.Printf("[audit] batch insert failed: %v", err)`, :70 `batch = batch[:0]`, :79 `if len(batch) >= 64 {`, :44 `l.db.Create(cl)` (return discarded), :46 `l.broadcastLive(cl)`. GORM semantics: gorm.io/gorm@v1.25.12 finisher_api.go:57-60 `if tx.SkipDefaultTransaction || reflectLen <= batchSize { tx.AddError(callFc(tx.Session(&Session{}))) } else { tx.AddError(tx.Transaction(callFc)) }`, and db.go:42-46 configures only Logger + TranslateError (SkipDefaultTransaction never set). Reachability: gateway.go:84 runs after gws.AuthMiddleware() (admin/routes.go:27-28, gateway.go:215-221 requires an enabled sk- key); behaviour is documented by gateway_test.go:164 `if got := resolveRequestID(mk("trace-abc-123")); got != "trace-abc-123" {`. No mitigation anywhere: repo-wide grep for `OnConflict|ErrDuplicatedKey|Ignore\(|Clauses\(` under backend/ = 0 hits; no per-row retry; no charset/length allowlist; metrics ring capped at 50 (metrics.go:77-79) and unrelated.
impact: A single authenticated tenant (one enabled API key) reusing one fixed X-Request-ID poisons the gateway's global audit writer. Its first row persists; every later duplicate makes audit.go:67 return `duplicated key not allowed`, and audit.go:70 throws the entire flush away — including 50..63 rows belonging to OTHER API keys — with no retry, no re-queue, and no operator-visible signal beyond a stderr line (audit.go:68). Verified empirically on the repo's exact driver stack (see 'empirical_verification'): 0/63, 0/39 and 0/28 co-flushed victim rows survive scenarios A/B/C respectively, and in scenario A even the first 50-row chunk that had already been inserted is rolled back by GORM's outer transaction (total rows after = 1, the seed). At >=5 poisoned requests/second (one per 200 ms tick) essentially every flush carries a collision, so gateway-wide call audit stops persisting entirely for the duration while all HTTP traffic continues normally. The attacker also evades its own persisted auditing (first-wins leaves only its stale seed row, which GET /api/admin/v1/audit/calls/:request_id returns via admin/audit.go:68 `s.db.Where("request_id = ?", reqID).First(&r)`), and because audit.go:46 broadcasts on ENQUEUE to the hub admin/auditws.go:72 serves, the live console keeps displaying the destroyed calls — so DB, CSV export (admin/audit.go:95-110), token/billing stats (admin/tokenstats.go:138-237) and dashboards (admin/dashboard.go:23-27, admin/models.go:202-205) all quietly understate or omit traffic while the operator sees 'everything handled'. Cross-tenant audit destruction is a privilege NO tenant role otherwise holds: there is no call-log delete/purge endpoint at all (routes.go:111-115 are GET-only; the only DELETE is the hourly retention sweep audit.go:102).
reason: Not refutable on evidence: all eleven quoted locations (gateway.go:84/306/311/272, model.go:248, audit.go:44/46/60/62/67-70/79, metrics.go:77-79) are exact, and the file cited + line 67 is the correct discard site. Not refutable on mechanism: the unique index demonstrably exists after AutoMigrate, the header is attacker-controlled with no normalisation, one CallLog row per request is written from the single deferred site at gateway.go:314-319 (so the chain needs the header reuse the finding describes, which is trivial), and a UNIQUE violation aborts the whole multi-row statement (SQLite ABORT) — plus GORM's transaction wrapper for 51..64-row flushes widens the loss to the entire flush, so the filed impact is if anything understated. Not refutable on trust boundary: the input is untrusted client input; the sole precondition (a valid API key) is the gateway's normal usage model, and the destroyed rows belong to other keys, so the 'attacker already has the privilege' break does not apply — no tenant, and no admin API, can delete call logs, and the actor gains no read primitive (so this is integrity/availability, not exfil). Not refutable on mitigations: no ON CONFLICT/insert-or-ignore, no per-row retry, no dedup, error ignored on both the batch path and the queue-full single-row fallback (probe E), and the live WS broadcast is structurally decoupled from persistence. Attack cost is lower than filed: a 400 from gateway.go:328-332 (or 348-362 / 370-376) still writes an audit row because gateway.go:257 `if status != "ok" { return true }` with CallAuditEnabled defaulting true (settings.go:33), and those early returns precede rate limiting (gateway.go:410) and quota (gateway.go:419), so the default rules cannot throttle the poison and it spends zero tokens and never touches an upstream. Severity stays high, not critical (authenticated actor; no RCE/authz-bypass/exfil) and not medium (not a hardening nicety but an actively exploitable, essentially free, self-masking destruction of the project's core audit control REQ-015/REQ-001). The 41..128-byte half of the finding is also accurate as written: probe D shows SQLite stores 128 chars untruncated (so no extra failure there, only unbounded growth until the hourly sweep), while on the postgres/mysql dialects db.go:28-39 supports, GORM's varchar(40) turns any oversized ID into a whole-flush failure with no duplicate required (MySQL non-strict would instead truncate and make distinct IDs collide).
exploit_sketch:
Precondition: one enabled gateway API key; nothing else.
1) SEED — `curl -X POST http://gw:8080/v1/chat/completions -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-<own-key>' -H 'X-Request-ID: healthcheck-0001' -d '{'`: gateway.go:84 accepts the header, gateway.go:328-332 rejects the body (400, before rate limit/quota/upstream), and the deferred gateway.go:314-319 still writes the audit row, which persists in the next flush as call_logs.request_id='healthcheck-0001'.
2) POISON — repeat the identical request. Each subsequent row collides with the seed, so audit.go:67 errors, audit.go:68 logs one line to stderr, audit.go:70 discards the whole queued batch — every other tenant's call rows in that 200 ms window (probe: 0 of 63/39/28 victims survive).
3) BLIND THE GATEWAY — sustain >=5 req/s: every flush now contains a poisoned row, so gateway-wide call audit stops persisting while all victim traffic still succeeds; the writer goroutine never dies (audit.go:63-71 just resets the slice), so no crash, no metric, no alert.
4) EVADE — the attacker's own later calls never land in the DB; the surviving seed is a benign-looking decoy row its fixed ID points at, returned by admin/audit.go:65-71, and the live WS console still streams all dropped calls (audit.go:46 -> admin/auditws.go:72) so the loss looks like normal traffic.
5) DIALECT VARIANT — on PostgreSQL or strict MySQL, a single `X-Request-ID` of 41..128 bytes fails the INSERT with value-too-long and kills the flush with no duplicate needed; on MySQL non-strict, 40-char truncation makes distinct long IDs collide spontaneously.

empirical_verification.harness: Standalone Go program written outside the repository (no project file modified), using the exact versions from backend/go.mod (github.com/glebarez/sqlite v1.11.0, gorm.io/gorm v1.25.12), gorm.Config{TranslateError: true} per db.go:42-46, SkipDefaultTransaction left false, AutoMigrate of a struct carrying the verbatim `gorm:"uniqueIndex;size:40"` tag, and CreateInBatches(batch, 50) per audit.go:67. Executed with go1.24.4 (GOTOOLCHAIN=local) against the local module cache via a file:// GOPROXY.
results: A: 64-row flush with a pre-existing seed and the duplicate at index 63 -> err `duplicated key not allowed`; rows in DB afterwards = 1 (seed only); victims persisted 0/63. Proves GORM's outer transaction rolls back the first, already-successful 50-row chunk.
B: 40-row flush (single multi-row INSERT statement), duplicate at index 20 -> victims persisted 0/39. Proves SQLite ABORT unwinds the whole statement, so loss is the entire flush even when n <= 50.
C: 30-row flush containing the duplicate pair with no prior row -> victims persisted 0/28, both attacker rows lost.
D: 128-byte request_id -> insert succeeds and stores 128 characters untruncated on SQLite (VARCHAR(40) is advisory there).
E: single-row fallback Create on a duplicate (audit.go:44) -> returns `duplicated key not allowed`, row not persisted, and Write() discards the value.

mitigations_checked: Verified present: no privilege escalation to a read path (audit read endpoints are JWT-admin only, routes.go:111-115); client IDs cannot collide with legitimately generated IDs unless the attacker fixes its own string (gateway.go:75-79 emits 32 hex chars); metrics/quota/last_used paths unaffected (metrics.go:76-79 ring cap; gateway.go:614/:768 consume quota separately); non-duplicate rows still persist on the queue-full fallback; 128-byte header cap bounds per-row growth on SQLite; writer survives errors. Verified ABSENT: ON CONFLICT / clause.OnConflict / INSERT OR IGNORE / ErrDuplicatedKey handling (0 grep hits); per-row retry or re-queue after audit.go:67; any length/charset validation of the header at gateway.go:84; any separation of a server-generated audit ID from the client correlation ID (same string feeds :308 response header, :514 upstream header, :629 SSE writer, :272 unique column); any failure metric/API/alert (stderr only); any dedup window. Also confirmed no pre-existing call-log purge endpoint that would make the destruction an already-held privilege.
recommendation: Adopt the filed recommendation, ordered: (1) stop letting client input own a unique column — persist `RequestID: newRequestID()` and store the client header in a new non-unique `client_request_id` column (size:128) so the response/upstream trace headers (gateway.go:308/:514) keep the passthrough behaviour; (2) regardless, never discard a flush: on a constraint/value error at audit.go:67, re-insert row-by-row (or clause.OnConflict{Columns: []clause.Column{{Name: "request_id"}}, DoNothing: true}) and retry the remainder, and surface a counter so the loss is not stderr-only; (3) enforce <=40 chars plus an [A-Za-z0-9._:-] allowlist in resolveRequestID to close the MySQL/Postgres value-too-long variant; (4) move l.broadcastLive(cl) (audit.go:46) so the live view reflects persisted rows, or mark broadcast rows as unconfirmed, and stop ignoring the error on the queue-full fallback at audit.go:44.
verification_notes: Files read end-to-end: audit.go (124L), gateway.go (831L), model.go:225-303, db.go (73L), routes.go (196L), admin/audit.go (204L), admin/auditws.go (120L), admin/middleware.go, admin/server.go, cmd/server/main.go, metrics.go:55-94, settings.go, gateway_test.go:153-213, plus gorm@v1.25.12 finisher_api.go:28-60. Full record: docs/security/raw/verify-gateway-1.json.

title: Amendment (strengthens gateway-1): the loss is not merely a failed 50-row statement — GORM wraps 51..64-row flushes in a transaction, and the poison costs zero tokens/quota because 400-level requests are audited before rate limit and quota run
evidence: finisher_api.go:57-60 (gorm v1.25.12, module cache) `if tx.SkipDefaultTransaction || reflectLen <= batchSize {` / `tx.AddError(callFc(tx.Session(&Session{})))` / `} else {` / `tx.AddError(tx.Transaction(callFc))`; SkipDefaultTransaction unset in db.go:42-46. Zero-cost path: gateway.go:257 `if status != "ok" {` / `return true` + settings.go:33 `CallAuditEnabled: true, CallAuditSampling: 1}` + gateway.go:312 initial `status: "error"` + gateway.go:328-332 early `return` before rate limiting at gateway.go:410 and quota at gateway.go:419.
impact: Widens the reported per-flush loss to the full 64-row window (including the chunk already inserted when the collision lands in the second chunk) and reduces the attack cost to a ~40-byte request that never reaches an upstream, is never rate-limited and never consumes quota — i.e. an unthrottleable poison.
reason: Recorded so the eventual fix is scoped correctly: patching only the 50-row chunk boundary would leave the transaction-wide rollback and the unthrottled error-path poison both intact.
exploit_sketch: Amends verify-gateway-1-1 steps 2 and 3 (no separate attack).
recommendation: No separate fix; covered by recommendation (1)+(2) of verify-gateway-1-1.
mitigations_checked: Rate limiting and quota cannot bound it (early-return paths skip both); no per-flush row cap below 64; MaxConnections (gateway.go:195) bounds concurrency but not request rate.

audit_item: adjacent observation surfaced while verifying gateway-1 (NOT part of that verdict)
title: OperationLog.IP is taken from an unvalidated X-Forwarded-For header, bypassing the TRUSTED_PROXIES stance and letting any JWT-authenticated admin forge the source IP recorded in operation audit
evidence: server.go:108-115 `func clientIP(c *gin.Context) string {` / `if v := c.GetHeader("X-Forwarded-For"); v != "" {` / `if i := strings.IndexByte(v, ','); i > 0 {` / `return strings.TrimSpace(v[:i])` / `}` / `return v` / `}` / `return c.ClientIP()` — the XFF branch wins before the proxy-aware c.ClientIP() is ever consulted. Sole consumer: server.go:95 `audit.LogOp(s.db, operatorOf(c), action, module, target, before, after, clientIP(c),`, i.e. model.go:280 `IP string `gorm:"size:64" json:"ip"`` of OperationLog, exported at admin/audit.go:181. Contrast: cmd/server/main.go:92 `if err := engine.SetTrustedProxies(cfg.TrustedProxies); err != nil {` with TRUSTED_PROXIES default empty (main.go:90-91 comment) makes c.ClientIP() deliberately TCP-peer-only, and the gateway honours that stance (gateway.go:222 `if !rec.IPAllowed(c.ClientIP()) {`).
impact: Operation-audit IP attribution — the field an investigator uses to correlate a destructive admin action (provider delete, backup restore, key revocation) with a source — is attacker-supplied for any authenticated admin (self-forged header) or for any anonymous caller of endpoints that reach recordOp. It does not bypass authentication or IP allowlists (the gateway path correctly uses c.ClientIP()), so it is integrity-of-metadata only, not an authz break.
reason: Filed separately and at low because it is outside the gateway-1 chain (different table, different actor: an authenticated admin rather than a tenant key holder) and grants no access — it only launders the IP column of operations the actor is already authorised to perform. It is real, locatable and contradicts the deployment's stated trusted-proxy posture, so it is worth a ticket rather than a downgrade to 'by design'.
exploit_sketch: Admin JWT in hand: `curl -X DELETE http://gw:8080/api/admin/v1/providers/7 -H 'Authorization: Bearer <jwt>' -H 'X-Forwarded-For: 203.0.113.9'` — routes.go:58 -> deleteProvider -> recordOp -> audit.LogOp stores IP=203.0.113.9 (admin/audit.go:181 exports it), while the real TCP peer appears only in the process access log at main.go:116-117.
recommendation: Use c.ClientIP() (which already honours SetTrustedProxies from main.go:92) for clientIP(), or gate the XFF branch on the request peer being a configured trusted proxy; log the raw header separately if needed.
mitigations_checked: engine.SetTrustedProxies(cfg.TrustedProxies) is correctly applied at main.go:92 but this helper ignores it; the gateway's IP allowlist (gateway.go:222) uses c.ClientIP() and is NOT spoofable (consistent with the architecture note); no rate-limit/lockout logic keys on clientIP() (grep: only server.go:95 consumes it), so impact is confined to audit metadata.
